items.title: Jack Teagarden Interview, 1959-10-29
items.q: Like the guy who worked with Jimmy Joy, Len Harrell, I'm talking about.

ctx.x: Well, he's self-taught, but he used to listen to, uh, everybody that came through Houston. Especially, there used to be quite a few colored boys that come through Houston, you know, from New Orleans. Yeah. And there was quite, quite a lot of, uh, entertainment in that city at that time. And, uh, I guess he picked up a little bit here and there from everybody and they put it all with his own. And, uh, it was fantastic when I first heard him and, uh, I guess he still is now. I saw him just a few weeks ago. I didn't…

You know, he seems to me to have been so wonderful and to develop a lot of things that, you know, from what I've heard from Len Harrell and guys who listen to him. Yeah. Yeah. Like the guy who worked with Jimmy Joy, Len Harrell, I'm talking about. Yeah. He must have heard a lot of classical music too, huh?

Yeah. He went, he made a, he made a real study of piano. He used to practice about eight hours a day. And, uh, he taught himself to read and then he, uh, went for Chopin mostly. And, uh, of course, uh, Debussy and, uh, and Ravel. And he made, uh, put all this with his ideas. And, uh, of course he knows Boogie Woogie and, uh, and the Earl Hines style of piano. He was playing long before, way before Earl Hines. And I guess it, uh, never been heard by anybody. He was sort of, uh, Art Tatum maybe. Uh, Art Tatum and…
